findings.title: run_steps honors the "report is still written" contract only for two exception types
findings.description: The module docstring promises "the first failure stops the run and the report is still written to `project-documents/user/notes/<date>-227-cutover.md`." `run_steps` (cutover_227_tick_backup.py) catches only `(StepFailed, subprocess.CalledProcessError)`. All *logical* failures go through `require()` → `StepFailed`, so those are fine. But the steps also perform unguarded I/O and parsing that raise other types: `step_check`/`main` call `CRON_FILE.read_text()`, and `step_production` reads `ctx.main.backup_root / "backup-health.log"` with no `exists()` guard (unlike the tick-side reads in `run_health`/`step_weekly`, which do guard). A `FileNotFoundError`/`PermissionError` there — or a `ValueError` from an `int()` parse in `tick_locks_held`/`health_flags` — propagates out of `run_steps` to `main()` *before* `report.write_text(...)`, so the run aborts with a bare traceback and **no cutover report**, contrary to the documented guarantee. For a one-shot production backup cutover whose only durable record is that report, the catch scope should cover the step bodies broadly (e.g. catch `Exception` and record it, or add the I/O/`ValueError` families) so the report is always written.

findings.title: `assert flags is not None` in run_health is unreachable and disappears under -O
findings.description: `run_health` calls `require(flags is not None, step, ...)` immediately before `assert flags is not None`. `require` raises `StepFailed` when `flags` is `None`, so the `assert` can never actually fire in a normal run — it is dead code. Its only observable effect is under `python -O`/`pytest -O`, where the assert is compiled out and `run_health` would then `return None` against a `tuple[int, int]` annotation (the `require` still prevents that, so no live bug, but the type contract becomes unsound). Delete the assert; `require` already enforces the invariant and is the thing `run_steps` actually catches.

findings.title: Production-diff guard re-spells the replication host and bucket as literals
findings.description: `strip_new_args`/`production_changes` hardcode `" --replication-host 127.0.0.1"` and `f" --remote {bucket_remote} "`, even though the parsed table row already exposes `ctx.main.replication_host` (and `ctx` carries `main`). The cutover reads `ctx.main.url_key` and `ctx.bucket_remote` but not `replication_host`, so the value is defined in `deploy/backup-clusters.conf` (the single source) yet re-spelled here. If the 17/main `replication_host` ever changes, `strip_new_args` will fail to strip the new value and `step_apply`'s "production lines changed beyond the new arguments" guard will report a spurious diff. Passing the host from the parsed row keeps the guard consistent with the table.

findings.title: Render substitution is patsub-replacement-safe and the production-preservation invariant is verified
findings.description: I verified the two invariants this change depends on. (1) Every `${x//pat/rep}` in `render_cron.sh` quotes `rep`, and `test_ampersand_survives_substitution` asserts each rendered job still ends in `2>&1` — so the bash 5.2 `&`-in-replacement pitfall the comment warns about is genuinely covered, not just commented. (2) `test_production_lines_gain_only_the_new_arguments` strips exactly the three new argument pairs from the rendered 17/main + host blocks and compares line-for-line against the pre-227 fixture, and `test_production_blocks_never_name_tick` confirms no tick path leaks into production's lines — the TD3 "production never moves" guarantee is mechanically enforced, not asserted in prose. The `@CLUSTER_BLOCKS@`-exactly-one-line guard and the unfilled-`@PLACEHOLDER@`/unescaped-`%` refusals also hold, so a bad render cannot reach `/etc/cron.d`.

structured_findings.summary: run_steps honors the "report is still written" contract only for two exception types
`assert flags is not None` in run_health is unreachable and disappears under -O
Production-diff guard re-spells the replication host and bucket as literals
Render substitution is patsub-replacement-safe and the production-preservation invariant is verified
